[ota-hal] OTA-1675: the voice names its step

Item two of "fix all existing issues one through six": #180, the voice-path
process kill on kai's SM-S942U (Samsung, SM8850, Android 16) — the first
non-Pixel kill on record. Like item one, this is the instrument, not the cure,
and it also repairs a defect in the instrument it extends.

WHAT HER LEDGER SAID
A cold 66-second life on the title screen, no action yet, model ledger o0/r0:

    native:voice:done [q0] · 66228ms into the action · alive 0ms after it
    Voice (TTS) guard: ⚠ VOICE CRASH detected — last voice: kokoro:bf_emma

The guard is armed by markTTSStart before the synth and cleared by markTTSDone
AFTER playback; so the process died between the synth settling and the line
finishing. Sixty-six seconds in, q0, o0/r0: that was the FIRST utterance that
device ever played — ReadyFlash speaks "Choose your character." the moment
Kokoro comes online. Nothing native runs in that window except what the voice
layer does with the samples: the WAV encode, expo-av's player load on a data:
URI (ExoPlayer → AudioTrack, the one step that is pure platform media code),
the playback, the deferred unload. OTA-1546 stamped the lock; nothing stamped
these. The owner's own two voice deaths (08-30 `native:voice:done (+11080ms)`,
08-31 `native:voice:start [q1]`) sit in the same blind spot.

AND THE INSTRUMENT ITSELF WAS ONE MICROTASK LATE
Measured in the new suite before it could be shipped: the lock's `done` stamp
rode the `.then` AFTER `task.resolve`, so the caller's continuation ran first.
The voice drain resumed, encoded the WAV and DISPATCHED the player load before
`native:voice:done` was written. Her last checkpoint said "the synth finished"
about a process that had already moved on to playback — and any checkpoint a
caller stamped in that continuation was overwritten by a fact from the step
before it, which is exactly what would have happened to the stamps below.
`done` is now stamped before the caller is resolved; it means the native op
settled, nothing more. Exclusivity is untouched — `running` still clears only
after the caller has been resolved. The ota1546 pin is repointed with the
reason.

THE PLAYBACK PATH STAMPS ITS OWN STEPS
`voice:play:encode` / `create` / `started` / `done` / `unload`, and
`voice:stop`, each carrying the utterance's ordinal in this life and its
length (`#1 0.2s`) — "the first line after a fresh model load" is the fact
that separates a one-off from a device that cannot play at all.

⚠ THE UNLOAD STAMP YIELDS. It fires 300 ms after the line ends, by which time
the lock may be inside the next synth or a Qwen job; overwriting
`native:llm:start` with `voice:play:unload` would file a death inside
inference as a death in a player release — the blind-spot trade OTA-1377 and
OTA-1413 refused. When the lock is running the crumb it wrote stands. Lazy-
required and wrapped, as the lock's own stamp is.

Not the cure. No exemption is bought with this. The next voice-path death
reads which step it died in.

- app/ai/nativeMlLock.ts — `done` stamped in the settle handlers, before
  resolve/reject.
- app/voice/PiperTTSManager.ts — `stampVoicePhase`, the per-life ordinal, the
  six stamps, the unload gate on `nativeMlSnapshot().running`.
- __tests__/ota1675TheVoiceNamesItsStep.test.ts — 16 tests: the whole window
  driven end to end through a mocked Kokoro + expo-av (load, warm-up, the
  line, then encode → create → started → done), the tag, the yield, voice:stop,
  the lock ordering measurement, and the source pins.
- __tests__/ota1546TheDyingBreathNamesTheNativeJob.test.ts — the order pin
  reads the settle handler.
